items.transcript: Okay, this is definitely going to be the [laughter] weirdest thing you see today. This is a real living cockroach with a tiny computer on its back running AI that helps steer it so that one day these things could like run through collapsed buildings and find people and things where robots normally can't. This is from the University of Osaka, and that's the Madagascar hissing cockroach with tiny wires in its antenna and well, its butt. A pulse to the antenna makes it turn, and a pulse to the rear makes it run. older systems steered them around every rock, even ones a roach could climb. So now the backpack can feel flat ground, a climb, a drop, or a hole. And it's right about 92% of the time. When a climb starts, the AI quits steering and lets the roach do its thing. Nobody had to like design new robot legs to make this work. Last year, Singapore sent 10 cyborg cockroaches into the rubble after the Myanmar earthquakes. Now, they didn't find anyone and Osaka's version is still in labs only. But still, this is pretty crazy and weird and also kind of cool. So, share this with a friend who loves weird tech and this science fiction type stuff. And don't forget to follow for more cool tech every single
